Cc: ops-eng@edgebridge.co

Subject: Satellite VPC deployment: orchestration & surface adjacency readout

Soojin / Marissa —

Thanks for taking time today. Attached is our current reference diagram (satellite_vpc_reference_v1.pdf) and a short runbook sketch for the Satellite footprint. Key asks for Redwood:

- Confirm control-plane placement options for the regional edge (single-zone control plane vs split-control nodes). We need guidance on HA behavior if we push control-plane components into the customer colocation pod.
- Clarify egress expectations for telemetry and KV cache replication (will prefer TLS over private peering where possible).
- Validate the orchestration handoff for canary cutover (we propose 30-min canary windows, 100rps burst).

Attached: satellite_vpc_reference_v1.pdf (diagram, 1.2MB)

Sanjay
Head of Infrastructure — EdgeBridge
sanjay@edgebridge.co

From: soojin_lee@redwood.example
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@edgebridge.co>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example, neha_kapoor@redwood.example
Date: 2029-11-27T13:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Satellite VPC deployment: orchestration & surface adjacency readout

On Tue, Nov 27, 2029 at 09:12, Sanjay Patel <sanjay@edgebridge.co> wrote:
> Soojin / Marissa —
>
> Thanks for taking time today. Attached is our current reference diagram...

Thanks, Sanjay — this is helpful. Quick readout from Redwood infra perspective:

- Control plane model: we recommend a split-control model for Satellite: lightweight control-plane agents in the customer pod, with a managed control-plane rendezvous in Redwood-managed region for leader election and version coordination. This minimizes blast radius while keeping rollout coordination centralized.
- Telemetry/egress: we can accept TLS-over-peering for metrics and traces. For KV replication we recommend a private mesh link (edge -> region) to avoid token sprawl; fallback to TLS if peering unavailable.
- Canary cadence: 30 mins looks fine; we'll propose a two-step canary (internal smoke + customer shadow traffic) and provide automatic rollback on error thresholds.

Action items for next week:
1) Marissa to validate control-plane startup sequence under cold boot (will attach controlplane_sequence.svg).
2) Neha to draft an egress proofing checklist and data retention constraints.
3) Sanjay to provide a staging VLAN range for NAT mapping.

I'll attach the basic checklist and a lean sequence diagram in the follow-up.

— Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.example
To: soojin_lee@redwood.example, Sanjay Patel <sanjay@edgebridge.co>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.example
Date: 2029-11-28T10:31:00Z
Subject: Re: Satellite VPC deployment: orchestration & surface adjacency readout

On Tue, Nov 27, 2029 at 13:04, soojin_lee@redwood.example wrote:
> Thanks, Sanjay — this is helpful. Quick readout from Redwood infra perspective...

Folks — I took a pass on the control-plane start sequence. A couple of clarifying Qs before I finalize the SVG:

1) Leader election: is the intent to run RAFT between lightweight paxos agents in-customer + region-leader, or to use the region as the source-of-truth only? RAFT across WAN can be fragile, so if we can limit consensus to region that reduces complexity.
2) KV cache replication frequency: EdgeBridge mentioned a 5s SLA for cache propagation. If that's correct we should quantify bandwidth and consider delta compression or quantized diffs.

I've attached controlplane_sequence.svg (SVG, 48KB) with inline notes. If RAFT is required, we need to confirm port ranges and whether customer firewall policy allows peer-to-peer 7000-7015.

Marissa
Director, Deployments | Redwood Inference

Attachment: controlplane_sequence.svg (diagram stub)

----

From: Emma Liu <emma@edgebridge.co>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example, soojin_lee@redwood.example
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@edgebridge.co>, ops-eng@edgebridge.co
Date: 2029-11-29T16:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Satellite VPC deployment: orchestration & surface adjacency readout

Marissa / Soojin —

Thanks for the notes. Quick answers:

- Leader election: we want region to remain source-of-truth; lightweight agents will register heartbeats and pull state from region. No WAN RAFT across customer pods.
- KV replication: target is near-real-time (<= 5s). We'll accept delta compression once you provide recommended protobuf diffs; current ops team prefers TLS-over-peering as first-class.
- Firewall: customer allowed 7000-7015 on staging VLAN; prod will require an ingress ticket but we can open a narrow range.

Also uploaded a short staging VLAN allocation and a DocuSign for our mutual NDA (link below).

Emma Liu
Cloud Platform — EdgeBridge

From: soojin_lee@redwood.example
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@edgebridge.co>, Emma Liu <emma@edgebridge.co>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example, neha_kapoor@redwood.example
Date: 2029-11-30T11:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Satellite VPC deployment: orchestration & surface adjacency readout

Thanks Emma — that's exactly what we needed. Attaching the deploy-readiness-checklist.xlsx (stub) with the proposed canary steps and rollback thresholds. Highlights:

- Preflight: firewall, NAT mapping, KMS connectivity, observability endpoints validated.
- Canary: 10% shadow for 15 mins -> 50% traffic ramp if no errors -> full cut after 30 mins stable.
- Rollback: immediate rollback on 5xx spike >0.5% or latency 95th >1500ms sustained for 3 sampling windows.

Next steps:
- Sanjay: confirm staging VLAN (we'll need the CIDR by EOD Friday).
- Marissa: I'll hand off control-plane cold-start tests to you on Monday.
- Neha: please prepare an egress proofing doc referencing retention SLA.

Attachments: deploy-readiness-checklist.xlsx (3 sheets)

— Soojin
